veranderings.blok: Van die rivier na die see
veranderings.voor: verdamp 'n deel van die water en 'n deel trek
veranderings.na: verdamp 'n deel van die water, en 'n deel trek
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb, so a comma goes before it.
In the sense of interlocking, 'inmekaar' is written as one word; 'in mekaar' means 'in each other'.

veranderings.voor: haal mense water uit en by die rivier
veranderings.na: haal mense water uit, en by die rivier
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: both clauses have their own subject and verb ('mense haal', 'dit gaan'), so a comma goes before 'en'.

veranderings.voor: Mense maak nie self water nie, maar leen
veranderings.na: Mense maak nie self water nie maar leen
veranderings.rede: The second half has no subject of its own (it shares 'Mense'), so under the AWS rule as briefed no comma goes before 'maar'.

vlae.teks: In tuine en op 'n boer se lande gaan 'n deel reguit in die lug of grond terug.
vlae.rede: The protected wording reads 'gaan 'n deel van die water reguit in die lug of die grond terug', but the lesson does not contain it in that form: 'van die water' and the second 'die' are missing. The meaning is the same, but the text does not match the protected entry, so a person should decide whether to restore it (3 more words, against the 400-word ceiling) or update the entry. Not a safety matter.
